content.user_title: Apply Marketing Psychology to Customer Decisions
content.value_statement: Marketing choices often fail when teams overlook how customers evaluate risk, value, and effort. This skill maps behavioral principles to ethical, practical recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Selects relevant mental models for specific marketing challenges.
Explains the psychology behind customer decisions in direct language.
Suggests applications for pricing, messaging, onboarding, conversion, retention, and growth.
Connects recommendations to the customer journey and current behavior barrier.
Distinguishes genuine scarcity from manufactured urgency.
limitations: Does not replace customer research, analytics, or controlled testing.
Does not guarantee conversion, retention, or revenue improvements.
Requires product and audience context for tailored recommendations.
Does not provide legal review for consent, pricing, or advertising practices.

use_cases.title: Improve SaaS Onboarding
use_cases.description: Apply behavior models to reduce friction, clarify choices, and encourage meaningful activation steps.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Pricing Communication
use_cases.description: Evaluate plan presentation, price framing, and value communication while preserving transparent customer choice.

use_cases.title: Develop Persuasive Campaigns
use_cases.description: Choose ethical persuasion principles for headlines, offers, testimonials, and calls to action.

prompt_templates.title: Explain One Principle
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain [psychological principle] and give three ethical marketing applications for [product type].
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn a principle before using it.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Customer Barrier
prompt_templates.prompt: Our customers hesitate at [journey stage]. Identify three relevant mental models and recommend one practical change for each.
prompt_templates.scenario: Connect behavior barriers to focused improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Marketing Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this [page or flow] for choice overload, friction, trust, and motivation. Prioritize five ethical improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Behavioral Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a behavioral strategy for [goal] using product context, customer beliefs, journey stage, constraints, safeguards, and measurable hypotheses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Develop an advanced, testable marketing plan.

output_examples.input: Customers abandon onboarding after choosing integrations.
output: Hick's Law suggests reducing visible integration choices.
Recommend a common setup first, with advanced options available later.
Measure completion rate and successful first actions.

output_examples.input: Explain ethical scarcity for a cohort course.
output_examples.output: Use the real enrollment deadline and actual seat limit. Explain the operational reason, and never reset the deadline for returning visitors.

output_examples.input: Review three SaaS pricing tiers for decision paralysis.
output: Clarify the customer profile for each plan.
Recommend a plan using documented fit criteria.
Remove overlapping features that make comparison difficult.

best_practices: Provide the product, audience, journey stage, and desired customer behavior.
Use psychological principles to clarify value while preserving informed choice.
Test recommendations with customer research and measurable experiments.
anti_patterns: Do not create fake scarcity, false social proof, or misleading anchors.
Do not assume a cognitive bias explains every customer decision.
Do not deploy recommendations without checking consent, accessibility, and legal requirements.

faq.question: What problems does this skill address?
faq.answer: It addresses customer hesitation, choice overload, weak value framing, onboarding friction, pricing perception, trust, retention, and growth strategy.

faq.question: Does it write complete marketing copy?
faq.answer: It can suggest psychological framing and examples, but a dedicated copywriting skill is better for complete production copy.

faq.question: Can it design an A/B test?
faq.answer: It can define behavioral hypotheses. Use an experimentation skill for sample planning, implementation, and statistical analysis.

faq.question: How does it support ethical marketing?
faq.answer: It favors real constraints, transparent claims, informed consent, and recommendations that preserve customer choice.

faq.question: What context produces the best results?
faq.answer: Provide the product, audience, current behavior, journey stage, customer beliefs, constraints, and available evidence.

faq.question: Does it guarantee better conversion rates?
faq.answer: No. Outcomes depend on the market, offer, execution, customer needs, and validation through research and testing.
